info.title: Coram API
info.description:
# Introduction

The Coram API enables seamless programmatic access to your security camera infrastructure, allowing you to build custom integrations and automate workflows.

# Supported Actions

Manage and interact with your Coram platform resources:

| Resource | Description |
| -------- | ----------- |
| **Camera Groups** | Organize and configure camera collections |
| **Cameras** | Access camera settings, streams, and metadata |
| **Locations** | Manage physical site configurations |
| **NVRs** | Control and monitor network video recorders |
| **Access Control** | Manage doors, cards, and permissions |

## Access Control

Card and permission changes are saved before they reach controllers. If a request fails, check the saved state before retrying.

# Required Headers

Every API request must include the following headers:

| Header | Required | Description |
| ------ | -------- | ----------- |
| `X-Auth-Token` | Yes | Your API key (from the API key List Page) |

**Example:**
```
curl -X GET "https://api.coram.ai/developer-api/v1/cameras" \
  -H "X-Auth-Token: xxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
```

# Response Format

All API responses follow a consistent structure based on the operation result.

## Success Response

**List Operations** (e.g., `GET /v1/cameras`)

Returns a `results` array with pagination support:

```json
{
  "results": [
    { "id": "cam_001", "name": "Front Door", ... },
    { "id": "cam_002", "name": "Lobby", ... }
  ],
  "has_more": true
}
```

When `has_more` is `true`, additional results are available. Use pagination parameters to fetch more.

**Bulk/Batch Operations** (e.g., `POST /v1/cameras`, `PATCH /v1/cameras`)

Returns a top-level `status` field indicating whether the API request was processed, and a `results` array where each item reflects the outcome of an individual operation:

```json
{
  "status": "success",
  "results": [
    { "status": "success", "data": { "id": "cam_001", "mac_address": "..." } },
    { "status": "error", "error": { "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR", "message": "..." } }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Description |
| ----- | ----------- |
| `status` (top-level) | `"success"` if the request was processed |
| `results[].status` | `"success"` or `"error"` for each operation |
| `results[].data` | Present when `status` is `"success"` |
| `results[].error` | Present when `status` is `"error"` |

## Error Response

When an error occurs, the response includes `status` set to `"error"` along with detailed error information:

```json
{
  "status": "error",
  "error": {
    "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
    "message": "Invalid MAC address format",
    "field": "mac_address"
  }
}
```

**Error Fields:**

| Field | Type | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ----------- |
| `code` | string | Machine-readable error code |
| `message` | string | Human-readable error description |
| `field` | string | The field that caused the error (if applicable) |


# HTTP Status Codes

The API uses standard HTTP status codes to indicate the success or failure of requests:

## Success Codes

| Code | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `200 OK` | Request succeeded |
| `201 Created` | Resource successfully created |
| `204 No Content` | Request succeeded with no response body |

## Client Error Codes

| Code | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `400 Bad Request` | Invalid request syntax or parameters |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Missing or invalid API key |
| `403 Forbidden` | Valid API key but insufficient permissions |
| `404 Not Found` | Requested resource does not exist |
| `422 Unprocessable Entity` | Validation error in request body |
| `429 Too Many Requests` | Rate limit exceeded |

## Server Error Codes

| Code | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `500 Internal Server Error` | Unexpected server error (rare) |
| `502 Bad Gateway` | Upstream service unavailable |
| `503 Service Unavailable` | Service temporarily unavailable |


# Error Handling Best Practices

1. **Always check the `status` field** — Verify if the response indicates `"success"` or `"error"`

2. **Handle specific error codes** — Use the `error.code` field to handle different error types programmatically

3. **Implement retry logic** — For `429` and `5xx` errors, implement exponential backoff

4. **Log error details** — Capture `error.code`, `error.message`, and `error.field` for debugging

**Example error handling:**
```python
response = api.create_camera(data)

if response["status"] == "error":
    error = response["error"]
    if error["code"] == "VALIDATION_ERROR":
        print(f"Invalid {error['field']}: {error['message']}")
    elif error["code"] == "DUPLICATE_RESOURCE":
        print("Camera already exists")
    else:
        print(f"Error: {error['message']}")
```

# Timeline Deep Links

You can construct a URL that opens the Coram web app on a camera's timeline at a specific past moment — for example, to link to footage from an incident record or an alert in your own system.

```
https://app.coram.ai/timeline/{camera_id}?ts={start_ms}&te={end_ms}
```

| Parameter | Location | Format | Description |
| --------- | -------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `camera_id` | path | integer | The camera's `id` as returned by List Cameras (`GET /v1/cameras`). Not the MAC address. |
| `ts` | query | Unix epoch milliseconds | Start of the playback window (absolute UTC instant). |
| `te` | query | Unix epoch milliseconds | End of the playback window. Must be greater than `ts`. |

**Example** — open camera `48389` at 2026-09-09 14:30:00 UTC with a 10-minute window:

```
https://app.coram.ai/timeline/48389?ts=1788964200000&te=1788964800000
```

## Behavior and Limitations

- Both `ts` and `te` are required. If either is missing or is not a valid millisecond timestamp, the page opens in live view instead.
- Timestamps are absolute instants. The timeline displays them in the camera's local timezone automatically.
- The link opens the Coram web app: the viewer must be signed in to your organization and have permission to view that camera's timeline. The link itself grants no access, but its URL does reveal the camera id and time window, so treat links as metadata your external systems may retain or forward.
- The requested window must fall within the camera's video retention period. A window outside retention shows an empty timeline.
- Use a window of at least a few minutes (in-app links use a 10-minute minimum) so the viewer has context around the moment of interest.

Timeline deep links are provided as-is and may change in a future release of the Coram web app.

---

# Getting Started

1. **Generate an API key** from your Coram app settings
2. **Explore the endpoints** in the navigation to begin integrating

Need help? Contact [support@coram.ai](mailto:support@coram.ai)

# Webhooks

Webhooks push events from Coram to your server as they happen, so you do not
have to poll. Register one endpoint per event type under
**Settings → Webhooks** in the Coram app. Webhook registration is not part of
this API.

Every delivery is an HTTP `POST` with a JSON body. Respond with any `2xx`
status as soon as you have accepted the event, and do the work afterwards.

## Event types

| Event type | Fires when | `data` payload |
| ---------- | ---------- | -------------- |
| `camera_alert` | An alert is triggered on a camera | `WebhookCameraAlertData` |
| `camera_alert_details` | The AI description and clip for a camera alert (clip is only populated for firearm alerts).  Always fires after camera alert webhook. | `WebhookCameraAlertDetailsData` |
| `alert_delivery_status` | An NVR's alert delivery status is first recorded, changes, or expires to unknown | `WebhookAlertDeliveryStatusData` |
| `device_status` | A camera or Coram Point goes online or offline | `WebhookDeviceStatusData` |
| `emergency_activated` | An emergency is activated | `WebhookEmergencyEventData` |
| `emergency_resolved` | An emergency is resolved | `WebhookEmergencyEventData` |
| `door_unlocked` | A door is unlocked | `WebhookAccessControlEventData` |
| `access_denied` | A credential is rejected at a door | `WebhookAccessControlEventData` |
| `door_forced_open` | A door is opened without authorization | `WebhookAccessControlEventData` |
| `door_held_open` | A door is held open past its threshold | `WebhookAccessControlEventData` |

`camera_alert` and `camera_alert_details` are two events for the same alert.
The first fires immediately. The second fires once the description and clip processing has
finished, and carries the payload of
`GET /v1/alerts/{alert_event_id}/details` plus `latency_ms` and
`invocation_latency_ms`. Match them on `alert_event_id`.

## Payload envelope

Every JSON webhook shares one envelope, with the per-event payload under
`data`:

```json
{
  "event_type": "camera_alert",
  "timestamp": "2024-01-01T12:00:00+00:00",
  "test": false,
  "tenant": "your-tenant-id",
  "text": "Camera Alert: Perimeter on Front Door at Main Building",
  "data": {
    "alert_name": "Perimeter",
    "camera_name": "Front Door",
    "location": "Main Building",
    "alert_type": "Trespasser",
    "camera_mac_address": "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF",
    "organization_name": "Acme Corp",
    "alert_event_id": 12345
  }
}
```

`text` is a human-readable summary of the event, which makes the payload
directly consumable by a Slack incoming webhook URL. `test` is `true` only
for deliveries triggered by the **Test** button in the app and never for real
events, so use it to keep test traffic out of production handling.

A `camera_alert_details` delivery carries the alert details payload instead:

```json
{
  "event_type": "camera_alert_details",
  "timestamp": "2024-01-01T12:00:30+00:00",
  "test": false,
  "tenant": "your-tenant-id",
  "text": "Camera Alert Details: alert 12345 on camera AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF",
  "data": {
    "alert_event_id": 12345,
    "alert_time": "2024-01-01T12:00:00+00:00",
    "camera_mac_address": "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF",
    "ai": {
      "status": "ready",
      "short_description": "A person approaches the front door.",
      "long_description": "A person in a dark jacket walks up to the front door and waits."
    },
    "clip": {
      "status": "ready",
      "mp4_url": "https://developer.coram.ai/v1/assets/clips/...",
      "expires_at": "2024-01-02T12:00:00+00:00"
    }
  }
}
```

`ai.status` is always terminal (`ready` or `failed`) on this event. The
webhook only fires once the description has settled, so you never receive
`pending` here. `clip` is omitted entirely when no clip is produced for the
alert, and `clip.mp4_url` expires 24 hours after it is issued.

## Alert delivery status

`alert_delivery_status` reports an NVR's `healthy`, `degraded`, or
`unknown` status on first creation and status changes, including recovery.
Same-status check-ins and old/equal observations send nothing. Registration
sends no snapshot; use `GET /v1/nvrs/status` for current state.

A 10-minute sweep marks subscribed tenants' health `unknown` after 15 minutes
without an accepted check-in. Detection typically takes 15–25 minutes, plus
processing/delivery delay; this is not an SLA. Records stale before registration
can notify. Missing/already-unknown records do not. A check-in before the sweep
can prevent expiry; missed transitions are not reconstructed.

Required data: `nvr` (NVR UUID), `status`, and `last_check_in_at` (backend receipt
time of the last accepted alert delivery status report, unchanged on expiry).
Envelope `timestamp` records the backend transition time; both timestamps use
RFC 3339 UTC. `text` summarizes the new status, for example
`Alert Delivery Status: coram-example is degraded`. This event is JSON-only.

Enqueueing is best effort after commit; failures can lose events without replay.
Queued deliveries use normal retries with unchanged body, timestamp, and delivery
ID. Customers should handle duplicates and out-of-order events using the
transition and check-in timestamps.

## Headers

Coram sets these on every delivery, and they cannot be overridden:

| Header | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` (`application/xml` for CAP XML emergency events) |
| `User-Agent` | `CoramAI/1.0` |
| `X-Webhook-Signature` | HMAC-SHA256 of the request body, hex-encoded |
| `X-Webhook-Delivery-Id` | A UUID that identifies the event. See below |
| `X-Webhook-Attempt` | The attempt number, starting at `1`. See below |

You can add up to 20 static custom headers per webhook in the app, which is
useful for an API key or a tracing header your endpoint requires. Header
names must be valid RFC 7230 tokens, and the following are reserved:
`content-type`, `content-length`, `user-agent`, `host`, `connection`,
`transfer-encoding`, `x-webhook-signature`, `x-webhook-delivery-id`,
`x-webhook-attempt`.

### Delivery id and attempt

`X-Webhook-Delivery-Id` identifies the event, not the HTTP request. Every
attempt of a delivery carries the same id. If Coram enqueues the same event
again, the new delivery carries the same id too, so one stored id is enough
to skip every repeat. Coram derives the id from the event, as follows:

| Event type | The id is the same for |
| ---------- | ---------------------- |
| `camera_alert`, `camera_alert_details` | One alert (`alert_event_id`) |
| `door_unlocked`, `access_denied`, `door_forced_open`, `door_held_open` | One access control event |
| `emergency_activated`, `emergency_resolved` | One emergency. Activation and resolution have different ids |
| `alert_delivery_status` | One status change of one NVR |
| `device_status` | One delivery only. Each status report gets a new id |

The id is unique per webhook event type, so `camera_alert` and
`camera_alert_details` for the same alert have different ids. Match those two
on `alert_event_id`. The **Test** button sends a new id on each click.

`X-Webhook-Attempt` is `1` on the first attempt of a delivery, `2` on the
first retry, and so on up to `7`. It counts the retries of one delivery
only. A delivery that Coram enqueues again starts at `1` with the same
delivery id, so do not use the attempt number to detect a repeat. Use it
for logging and alerting. The **Test** button does not send this header.

## Verifying the signature

`X-Webhook-Signature` is the hex-encoded HMAC-SHA256 of the **raw request
body bytes**, keyed with your webhook's secret. Compute it over the bytes as
received. Parsing and re-serializing the JSON changes them and the signature
will not match. Always compare with a constant-time function, and reject a
missing or malformed header rather than letting the comparison raise. Both
constant-time primitives below throw on inputs an unauthenticated caller
controls.

```python
import hashlib
import hmac

def is_signature_valid(
    raw_body: bytes, header_signature: str | None, secret: str
) -> bool:
    if not header_signature:
        return False
    expected = hmac.new(
        key=secret.encode("utf-8"),
        msg=raw_body,
        digestmod=hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()
    # Compare as bytes: compare_digest raises TypeError on a non-ASCII str.
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected.encode(), header_signature.encode())
```

```javascript
import crypto from "node:crypto";

function isSignatureValid(rawBody, headerSignature, secret) {
  if (typeof headerSignature !== "string") return false;
  const expected = Buffer.from(
    crypto.createHmac("sha256", secret).update(rawBody).digest("hex"),
    "utf8",
  );
  const received = Buffer.from(headerSignature, "utf8");
  // timingSafeEqual throws on a length mismatch, so check the lengths first.
  if (received.length !== expected.length) return false;
  return crypto.timingSafeEqual(expected, received);
}
```

Your secret is shown when you create the webhook and can be regenerated in
the app. Regenerating takes effect immediately, and deliveries signed with
the previous secret stop at that point.

## Delivery semantics

| Property | Behaviour |
| -------- | --------- |
| Timeout | 5 seconds for each attempt, from connecting to reading your response |
| Redirects | Not followed, so a `3xx` counts as a failed attempt |
| Retries | Up to 7 attempts. See below |
| Guarantee | At least once while retries last. Deduplicate on `X-Webhook-Delivery-Id` |
| Ordering | Not guaranteed. Use `timestamp` to order events |
| Destination | Must be a publicly resolvable address. Private and loopback addresses are rejected |

### Retries

An attempt fails on any response other than `2xx`, on a timeout, or on a
network error. After a failed attempt Coram tries again, up to 7 attempts in
total. The waits between attempts are 5 s, 15 s, 30 s, 60 s, 120 s and
300 s, so the last attempt comes about 9 minutes after the first. If that
attempt also fails, the event is dropped.

Each attempt sends the same body bytes with the same `X-Webhook-Delivery-Id`.
It reads the webhook's URL, secret and custom headers again, so a change you
make in the app applies from the next attempt. If you delete the webhook,
the retries stop.

The **Test** button in the app sends a single attempt and does not retry.

### Duplicates and ordering

Coram can deliver the same event more than once. This happens when your
endpoint processes a request but the response does not reach Coram in time.
Store the `X-Webhook-Delivery-Id` values you have handled and skip a
repeat.

Events can arrive out of order, because a retried event can arrive after a
newer one. Order events by the envelope `timestamp`, not by arrival time.
`camera_alert_details` for an alert can also arrive before its
`camera_alert` when the first `camera_alert` attempt fails.

Acknowledge first and process asynchronously. A slow handler times out, and
Coram then sends the event again.

## Emergency events

`emergency_activated` and `emergency_resolved` deliver **CAP 1.2 XML** by
default, not the JSON envelope above, so an integration built for the JSON
events will not parse them as-is. Switch the webhook's response format to
JSON in the app if you want the standard envelope with
`WebhookEmergencyEventData` under `data`.

get.description: Returns a public download URL for the MP4 video clip associated with an alert event. The URL does not require authentication and expires after 24 hours. Use the alert_event_id from webhook payloads to retrieve the corresponding video clip.

Returns the current feedback (0.0-1.0 rating, reason, comment) for a firearm alert event. Feedback is organization-wide (last write wins); the feedback fields are null when no feedback has been submitted yet. Returns 404 if the alert event does not exist and 400 if it is not a firearm alert.

put.description: Submits feedback for a firearm alert event. rating is a 0.0-1.0 score (today 0.0 = incorrect / unhelpful, 1.0 = correct). Feedback is organization-wide and idempotent (last write wins): submitting again replaces the previous feedback. feedback_reason and feedback_comment are optional. Returns 404 if the alert event does not exist and 400 if it is not a firearm alert.

get.description:
Returns metadata about an alert event, including the rich natural-language description generated by Coram's vision language model. The description is produced asynchronously after the alert webhook fires, so consumers polling immediately may see `ai.status: pending` for a few seconds. Once `ai.status` is `ready`, the `ai.short_description` and `ai.long_description` fields are populated. If it is `failed`, no description will arrive.

When a video clip is being produced for the alert, a `clip` object is included: `clip.status` is `ready` (with a download `mp4_url` valid for 24 hours and an `expires_at`), `pending` (still uploading — poll again shortly), or `failed`. Alerts with no clip pipeline omit the `clip` field entirely.

Returns a paginated list of the firearm-detection alert configurations your key can access, ordered by firearm_alert_id. A key created by a user with restricted camera access only lists alerts on the cameras that user can see. Each entry has the same shape the create and update endpoints return.

403.description: Unauthorized

post.description: Creates a firearm-detection alert configuration. Recipients are specified by email (matched case-insensitively) and resolved to platform users in your organization; each recipient's notify_by_sms/notify_by_push only deliver when the user has a phone number / registered device. The schedule is interpreted in each camera's local time. The alert is attributed to the API key (creator_name = the key's identity). Note: a null name is omitted from the response rather than serialized as null.

403.description: Unauthorized

get.description: Returns a single firearm-detection alert configuration. Responds 404 if the firearm alert does not exist in your organization or your key cannot access its cameras. Note: a null name is omitted from the response rather than serialized as null.

403.description: Unauthorized

delete.description: Deletes a firearm-detection alert configuration and any alerts it has produced. Returns 204 on success and 404 if the firearm alert does not exist in your organization.

403.description: Unauthorized

patch.description: Partially updates a firearm-detection alert configuration; only the provided fields are changed. Providing recipients replaces the full recipient list. The schedule is interpreted in each camera's local time. Note: a null name is omitted from the response rather than serialized as null.

403.description: Unauthorized

get.description:
List all cameras accessible to the user.

Retrieve cameras accessible to the user with their current status and
configuration details. Results can be filtered by NVR, location,
MAC address, IP address, or camera group ID.

post.description:
Register multiple cameras in single location.

Register one or more cameras at a location by assigning them to available NVRs.
Cameras are automatically load-balanced across NVRs based on available capacity.

delete.description:
Delete one or more cameras.

Remove one or more cameras from the system.

patch.description:
Update one or more cameras.

Update configuration, credentials, feature flags, and group assignments
for one or more cameras. Each camera is updated independently - if one
camera's update fails, others can still succeed. Within each camera's
update, all changes are atomic.

**Group Assignment:**
- Provide `group_ids` to assign the camera to specific groups
- An empty list `[]` resets the camera to the default group
- Omit `group_ids` (null) to leave group assignments unchanged

**IP Address:**
- Provide `ip` to change the address the NVR connects to; it takes effect
  within a few minutes without any action on the NVR
- The change applies to every head of a multi-head camera
- On NVRs with automatic network scan enabled, discovery overrides the
  value if it does not match the IP the camera is actually reachable at

post.description:
Delete one or more cameras.

Equivalent to `DELETE /v1/cameras` for clients that cannot send a request
body with DELETE.

Move one or more cameras to different NVRs.

Transfer one or more cameras from one NVR to another.

get.description:
List camera groups.

Retrieve a paginated list of camera groups.
Groups are used to organize cameras for easier management and access control.

post.description:
Create a new camera group.

Create a new camera group with the specified name. Camera groups are used
to organize cameras for easier management and access control.

403.description: Unauthorized

get.description:
List all NVRs accessible to the user.

Retrieve NVRs accessible to the user with their current status and
configuration details. Results can be filtered by NVR UUID or location.

post.description:
Register multiple NVRs in bulk.

Register one or more NVRs by assigning them to locations.

Run ping test on NVR.

Send a ping request to the specified NVR to test network connectivity.

Run speed test on NVR.

Initiate a speed test on the specified NVR to measure network performance.

get.description:
List all locations accessible to the user.

Retrieve locations accessible to the user for the organization.
Returns locations across all product lines the user has access to.

403.description: Unauthorized

post.description:
Create multiple locations in bulk.

Create one or more locations for the organization.

get.description: Returns a public download URL for the MP4 video clip captured by the event's door's primary camera around the event timestamp. The URL does not require authentication and expires after 24 hours. Use the event_id from the events list endpoint or a webhook payload to fetch the clip.

Returns status for authorized NVRs in UUID order. Requires read:* scope
and at least LIVE_ONLY surveillance access. Full-access users see every
tenant-owned NVR, including devices without a location. Restricted users
see NVRs at their allowed locations or camera-group locations.
Status combines independent data sources and is not an atomic snapshot.
Invalid or unavailable uptime is null; required database failures fail
the request. Unknown or inaccessible NVR identifiers return an empty collection.

parameters.name: X-Tenant-User
parameters.description: Required for privileged global:read keys; the email of a user whose surveillance tenant access determines the target org.

parameters.name: X-Tenant-Org
parameters.description: Optional org selection with X-Tenant-User and global:read. The named user's surveillance access to this org is verified.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: One-based page number. Offset overflow is rejected.

parameters.name: nvr
parameters.description: Exact NVR identifier, applied before pagination. Empty is treated as absent.

400.description: Invalid query parameters or tenant selection.

401.description: API key is missing, invalid, revoked, or expired.

403.description: API key lacks the required permissions or access to the requested organization.

404.description: The user specified in X-Tenant-User was not found.

429.description: Too many requests. Try again later.

500.description: Failed to retrieve NVR status data.

get.description:
Returns current aggregate CPU utilization for authorized NVRs in UUID order. Requires read:* scope
and at least LIVE_ONLY surveillance access. Full-access users see every
tenant-owned NVR, including devices without a location. Restricted users
see NVRs at their allowed locations or camera-group locations.
CPU uses the Grafana five-minute rate calculation across available modes,
excluding idle and I/O-wait from the numerator. Invalid, stale or unavailable
telemetry is null; required database failures fail the request. Unknown or
inaccessible NVR identifiers return an empty collection. Pagination is not
a snapshot across inventory changes. Clients must tolerate additive fields.

parameters.name: X-Tenant-User
parameters.description: Required for privileged global:read keys; the email of a user whose surveillance tenant access determines the target org.

parameters.name: X-Tenant-Org
parameters.description: Optional org selection with X-Tenant-User and global:read. The named user's surveillance access to this org is verified.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: One-based page number. Offset overflow is rejected.

parameters.name: nvr
parameters.description: Exact NVR identifier, applied before pagination. Empty is treated as absent.

400.description: Invalid query parameters or tenant selection.

401.description: API key is missing, invalid, revoked, or expired.

403.description: API key lacks the required permissions or access to the requested organization.

404.description: The user specified in X-Tenant-User was not found.

429.description: Too many requests. Try again later.

500.description: Failed to retrieve NVR metrics data.

get.description:
Returns the doors the API key creator can see, with their online
status. Admins see every door in the tenant; lower roles see only
doors they have permission to unlock. Use `page` and `limit` to
paginate; `has_more` on the response signals more pages remain.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-indexed page number.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum doors per page (capped at 100).

403.description: API key lacks the required scope or role

get.description:
Returns events emitted by access control devices: card scans
(`card_reader_event`), grant/deny decisions (`access_control_event`),
REX presses (`rex_event`), door-held-open alarms (`door_held_open_event`),
battery alerts, and so on. Use the filters to narrow down by door,
cardholder, event type, or time window. Pagination uses the same
`page` + `limit` + `has_more` shape as every other developer-API list
endpoint.

The per-event `details` object carries event-type-specific data
(card_id, access_decision_reason, etc.). Treat it defensively: new
keys may appear in future event types.

parameters.name: start_time
parameters.description: RFC3339 inclusive lower bound on `timestamp`.

parameters.name: end_time
parameters.description: RFC3339 inclusive upper bound on `timestamp`.

parameters.name: door_ids
parameters.description: Repeat to filter to events emitted at specific doors.

parameters.name: cardholder_ids
parameters.description: Repeat to filter to events for specific cardholders.

parameters.name: event_types
parameters.description: Repeat to filter to a subset of event types.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-indexed page number.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum events per page (capped at 100).

403.description: API key lacks the required scope

post.description:
Sends a momentary-unlock command to the door's controller board.

post.description:
Imports a reunification roster as JSON. This is the API
equivalent of the in-app CSV upload and writes to the same roster.

**Every call replaces the whole roster.** Records you send are created
or updated, and anything you leave out is deleted. Only records that
came from this API or the in-app CSV upload are replaced.

Deleting someone revokes the Coram access an earlier import gave them.
Access granted by hand survives. Revocation is also skipped when a previous
import has not finished creating accounts yet, and when more than half
of a provisioned roster of 10 or more people would lose access at once,
which stops a truncated upload locking out a school.

Send every key on every call. The one you may omit is `staff`, and
omitting it deletes every staff member.

The import aborts and leaves the old roster intact if two schools map to
the same Coram location, if a location id does not exist, or if a
student or teacher repeats a school id in `school_ids` after the first
one. Repeating a `student_id`, `teacher_id` or `staff_id` returns `400`
before any work starts.

The order of the top level arrays does not matter.

The import runs in the background and is cancelled after one hour. The
`202` carries the initial status. Poll
`GET /v1/reunification/imports/status`. One import runs per organization
at a time and the in-app CSV upload counts as one, so a second request
returns `409`.

Requires `write:*` scope and an `admin` creator role. The status
endpoint needs `read:*`, so a write-only key can start an import but
never see whether it worked. Requests are limited to an average of 5
per second with a short burst allowance, and the body to 32 MiB.

400.description: Body is not a JSON object, omits or nulls any of schools/students/teachers/sections, has an empty school_location_mappings, repeats a student/teacher/staff id, or exceeds 32 MiB

403.description: API key lacks the required scope/role

409.description: An import is already running for this organization, including one started by the in-app CSV upload. Poll the existing one instead. The lock clears after one hour at the latest

get.summary: Get the current reunification import status
get.description:
Returns the status of your organization's most recent reunification
import. Poll this after starting one. Requires `read:*` scope and a
`regular` creator role.

Status is kept for one hour after its last update and then this returns
`404`. Store anything you need to keep.

`completed` means the roster was written and account provisioning was
handed to a background worker, not that every account exists.
`succeeded_users` and `failed_users` keep rising afterwards, which can
take several minutes on a large roster, so poll until both stop moving.

The `synced_*` and `total_*` pairs are a progress bar rather than a
success ratio. They end up equal whenever the roster is written, so they
cannot tell you a record was rejected.

A `failed` status does not mean the roster is untouched. If the failure
came after the roster was committed the new roster is live, and account
provisioning may not have started or may already be under way.

403.description: API key lacks the required scope/role

404.description: No import found for this organization, or the status expired. Status is kept for one hour after its last update

get.description:
Returns the organization's firearm alert events raised in a time window,
newest first. Both `start_time` and `end_time` are required and the
window may span at most 7 days. Pagination uses the same `page` +
`limit` + `has_more` shape as every other developer-API list endpoint.

Each result has the shape `/alerts/{alert_event_id}/details` returns,
with the AI description and the clip. This list never starts a clip
download. Where `/details` would request one, the `clip` here reads
`pending` for 5 minutes after the alert and `failed` after that. The
list leaves out alert events waiting for or failing AI verification.

parameters.name: start_time
parameters.description: RFC3339 inclusive lower bound on `alert_time`.

parameters.name: end_time
parameters.description:
RFC3339 inclusive upper bound on `alert_time`. Must not be before
`start_time` or more than 7 days after it.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-indexed page number.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum alert events per page (capped at 100).

400.description: A time bound is missing or not RFC3339, the window is longer than 7 days, or a pagination value is invalid

403.description: API key lacks the required scope or role

get.description:
Streams the alert's clip as MP4 bytes. Use this when you want the video
itself; use `GET /v1/alerts/{alert_event_id}/clip` instead when you want
a temporary URL you can hand to a player or another system.

Supports HTTP `Range` requests, so players can seek without downloading
the whole file. To learn a clip's size without fetching it, send
`Range: bytes=0-0` and read the total from `Content-Range`.

Batch-generated clips are retained for 7 days after the alert.
Streaming-generated clips are available through this endpoint for 1
hour because their readiness marker expires before the stored object.
Anything else — the clip was never requested, the upload has not
finished, or the applicable availability window has passed — returns
404.

parameters.name: alert_event_id
parameters.description: The alert event to download the clip for.

206.description: The requested byte range of the clip, when a `Range` header was sent.

400.description: The alert event ID is outside the supported integer range

403.description: API key lacks the required scope or role

404.description: No clip available for this alert

405.description: The endpoint only supports GET requests

get.description:
Returns the alert's image as JPEG bytes. For firearm and PPE alerts this
is the full-resolution frame the detection ran on; for every other
camera alert it is the stored alert image, which is the detection crop.

Pass `size=medium` or `size=small` to receive a re-encoded image
bounded to roughly 128 KB or 64 KB; resized responses ignore Range
requests.

Returns 404 when the alert has no image — it is not a camera alert, or
the object has already been deleted from storage.

parameters.name: alert_event_id
parameters.description: The alert event to download the image for.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description:
Target size of the returned image. `full` returns the stored image
unmodified. `medium` re-encodes to roughly 128 KB and `small` to
roughly 64 KB; an image already within the target is returned
unmodified. When omitted, a server-configured default applies
(currently `full`).

400.description: The alert event ID is outside the supported integer range, or the size value is not one of small, medium, full

403.description: API key lacks the required scope or role

404.description: No image available for this alert

405.description: The endpoint only supports GET requests

`schools`, `students`, `teachers` and `sections` must be present, and may
be empty arrays. Sending one as `null` is rejected the same way as leaving
it out, because both would wipe everything that key covers. Only `staff`
may be left out entirely.

Phone numbers are normalized to E.164 against the deployment's own
region, currently the United States. A number that cannot be parsed is
stored as null rather than rejected, so include a country code.

Unrecognized keys are dropped without error, so a misspelled field name
fails silently.

sections.description: An empty array removes every student to teacher pairing on the roster.

school_location_mappings.description: Maps your school ids to Coram location IDs. Must be present and non-empty. Give every school an entry, because a school without one is imported with no location and everyone attached only to it loses access. Two schools may not point at the same location, and a location that does not exist in your organization aborts the import after it has already returned 202. The location id in the example is illustrative, so look up your real ones with `GET /v1/locations` before your first call.

school_id.description: Your identifier for the school, referenced by students, teachers, staff and school_location_mappings. A blank value drops the school silently, and with it every reference to it. Do not send the same school_id twice.

name.description: Not validated. A blank name is accepted and shows as a nameless school in Coram.

sis_id.description: Stored and displayed only. Nothing matches or de-duplicates on it.

ReunificationSection.description: A class that pairs students with teachers. Sections build those pairings and are not stored as records you can look up later.

section_id.description: Must not be blank or the section is dropped. Never stored, so nothing can look it up.

school_id.description: Accepted and ignored. Sections take their schools from the people in them.

teacher_ids.description: A teacher id that does not resolve drops that teacher's pairings in this section without error.

student_ids.description: A student id that does not resolve drops that student's pairings in this section without error.

ReunificationStaff.description: Omitting the whole staff array deletes every staff member on the roster.

staff_id.description: A blank value drops the staff member silently.

email.description: Without a valid one the staff member is still imported but gets no Coram account and loses any access an earlier import gave them.

roles.description: Free text, not a fixed set. Displayed in Coram and used for nothing else.

school_ids.description: Unlike students and teachers, repeated ids here are removed rather than aborting the import. Staff have no primary school.

student_id.description: Your identifier for the student. A blank value drops the student silently. Stored as the student's card number and visible in Coram, so do not put anything sensitive here.

name.description: Not validated. A blank name is accepted and stored empty.

sis_id.description: Stored and displayed only. Nothing matches or de-duplicates on it.

email.description: The identity Coram uses for this person. They are still imported and still counted without a valid one, but they get no Coram account, appear in neither user counter, and lose any access an earlier import gave them. Two people sharing an email collapse into one Coram account.

school_ids.description: Schools the student belongs to, in order. The first one that resolves becomes the primary school, so a typo in the first position silently promotes the next. Repeating that first id is ignored, but repeating any other aborts the whole import. A student whose school_ids all fail to resolve is imported with no location access.

ReunificationGuardian.description: Guardians are contacts only and never receive a Coram account. Two guardians sharing an email address, or a phone number when there is no email, are merged into one guardian across the whole payload.

name.description: A guardian with a blank name is discarded along with their contact details.

relationship.description: Free text. Stored as "Other" when omitted or blank.

teacher_id.description: A blank value drops the teacher silently.

email.description: Without a valid one the teacher is still imported but gets no Coram account and loses any access an earlier import gave them.

school_ids.description: The first one that resolves becomes the primary school. Repeating that first id is ignored, but repeating any other aborts the whole import.

ReunificationImportStatus.description: Progress report for your most recent import. Counters that are zero are left out of the response, so treat an absent field as zero. Every counter resets when a new import starts.

total_guardians.description: Counted after the merge described on the guardian object, so it is usually lower than the number of guardian entries you sent.

succeeded_users.description: Coram accounts created or updated. Rises in the background after status becomes completed. Guardians are never included, because they get no account.

failed_users.description: Accounts that could not be created, usually a seat limit or an Auth0 rejection. Zero does not mean everyone succeeded, since anyone without a valid email is absent from both figures.

started_at.description: Carries a real time only while the import is in progress. Once it reaches completed or failed the field is still returned but reset to 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z, so record the start time yourself if you need it.

completed_at.description: Returned as 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z until the import finishes.

WebhookEvent.description:
Envelope every JSON webhook delivery shares. The per-event payload is
carried under `data`. See the Webhooks section of the introduction for
which payload each event type carries.

test.description: True only for deliveries triggered by the Test button in the Coram app. Never true for real events.

tenant.description: Identifier of the Coram organization the event belongs to.

text.description: Human-readable summary of the event. Makes the payload directly consumable by a Slack incoming webhook URL.

data.description: Event payload. Its shape is determined by `event_type`.

WebhookEventType.description: Event types a webhook can be registered for.

last_check_in_at.description: Backend receipt time of the last accepted NVR alert delivery status report (UTC); unchanged on expiry.

alert_event_id.description: ID of the alert event. Use it to correlate with the `camera_alert_details` event and to retrieve the alert via `GET /v1/alerts/{alert_event_id}/details`.

latency_ms.description: Server-measured milliseconds from alert trigger to right before the webhook HTTP request is issued.

invocation_latency_ms.description: Server-measured milliseconds spent in Coram's webhook pipeline for this alert. A subset of `latency_ms` covering only the webhook path.

metadata.description: Alert-type-specific details. Populated for firearm alerts, null for every other alert type.

WebhookFirearmAlertMetadata.description: Firearm-specific details of a `camera_alert`. Classification is best-effort and carries no accuracy guarantee.

gun_type.description: Type of firearm detected: `hand_gun` or `long_gun`. Null when the detection pipeline does not classify it.

gun_stance.description: How the firearm is held: `high ready`, `low ready`, `inactive carry` or `object holstered` (`none` when not determined). Null when the detection pipeline does not classify it.

bbox.description: Bounding box of the person carrying the firearm (not the firearm itself). Null when unavailable.

WebhookAlertBoundingBox.description: Bounding box normalized 0-1 on the full camera frame, origin top-left.

x_min.description: Left edge, 0-1 of the frame width.

y_min.description: Top edge, 0-1 of the frame height.

x_max.description: Right edge, 0-1 of the frame width.

y_max.description: Bottom edge, 0-1 of the frame height.

WebhookCameraAlertDetailsData.description: Payload of the `camera_alert_details` event. The alert details endpoint's response plus two server-measured latency fields that only a pushed event can report.

latency_ms.description: Server-measured milliseconds from the alert trigger (`alert_time`) to right before the webhook HTTP request is issued. This event waits for the AI description and, for firearm alerts, the video clip to settle, so the value is dominated by that wait.

invocation_latency_ms.description: Server-measured milliseconds Coram spent on the work needed to fire this webhook, up to right before the HTTP request is issued. A subset of `latency_ms` excluding the wait for the description and clip to settle.

device_status.description: The status the devices changed to.

devices.description: Devices affected by this status change.

WebhookDevice.description: A single device in a `device_status` event.

WebhookEmergencyEventData.description: Payload of the `emergency_activated` and `emergency_resolved` events. Only delivered when the webhook's response format is set to JSON. The default is CAP 1.2 XML.

WebhookAccessControlEventData.description: Payload shared by the `door_unlocked`, `access_denied`, `door_forced_open` and `door_held_open` events. Per-event extras are optional fields. `actor_*` appears on `door_unlocked` and `access_denied`, and `reason` on `access_denied`.

event_id.description: ID of the underlying access-control event. Use it to fetch the event's video clip via `GET /v1/access-control/events/{event_id}/clip`.

door_id.description: ID of the door the event was emitted on.

location_id.description: ID of the location the door belongs to, if any.

actor_user_id.description: Coram user_id that initiated the action, if known.

actor_card_id.description: Card credential id used, if the actor was a card holder.

reason.description: Controller's denial reason for `access_denied` events (e.g. 'card_not_recognized', 'outside_schedule', 'card_disabled'). Null on other event types.
